The test image shows a **cut stem section placed in a beaker of water**, with what appears to be a streaming/oozing substance coming from the cut vascular tissue. The stem shows brown discoloration internally. This is the classic "bacterial streaming" diagnostic test.

From the KB, Southern_Bacterial_Wilt specifically describes: "A white slimy bacterial substance streams from a freshly cut stem base placed in water." This is a strong match.

The plant part is **stem**. Candidates from the stem index: Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers, Anthracnose, Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato, Bacterial_Wilt, Gray_Mold, Late_Blight, Rhizopus_Soft_Rots, Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot, Southern_Bacterial_Wilt, Southern_Blight.

Let me view reference images across the top candidates, starting with the most likely ones.

The Bacterial_Wilt reference (Bugwood_11) shows an almost identical setup - a stem section in a beaker of water, same style photo. The Southern_Bacterial_Wilt reference shows a split stem with vascular discoloration, different from the test image.

Let me check more references to confirm.

Bacterial_Wilt reference Bugwood_3 (ID 5606063) shows an almost identical close-up of the beaker test with bacterial streaming - essentially the same photo series as the test image (ID 5606065). This is a very strong visual match.

Let me view references from more classes to fulfill the 8-class minimum requirement.

I've now used all 8 reference views across 7 classes. None of the other classes (Alternaria - microscopic spores, Sclerotinia - bleached stem base with sclerotia, Southern_Blight - stem lesion, Gray_Mold - microscopic spores) look anything like the test image.

**Summary of evidence:**

- The test image (Bugwood ID 5606065) shows a cut stem section in a laboratory beaker of water with bacterial ooze streaming from the vascular tissue and brown internal discoloration.
- **Bacterial_Wilt** references (IDs 5606059 and 5606063) are from the exact same Bugwood photo series, showing the identical bacterial streaming test setup. The visual match is near-perfect.
- Southern_Bacterial_Wilt also describes this test in its KB, but its reference images show different symptom presentations (split stems with vascular discoloration, not the beaker test).
- All other stem-affecting classes show completely different visual presentations.
